title: bug: moe-account-switch's scheduled /exit never runs while Claude Code waits for the usage limit to reset, so an interactive seat stalls until the reset
description:
This follow-up to task-05e1f916 (DONE 10-26) was observed 2026-11-02. Its turn.complete fallback fires, but the /exit it schedules does not end the session.

**What happened.** architect-d54b05fd ran an interactive TUI, pid 890235, with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR acct-2, holding VSC-17 (task-6a0f0be3) in PLANNING. Its transcript is acct-2 projects/-mnt-d-projexts-moes/401f548a-84e4-494d-a53f-ffea2a582e31.jsonl, lines 1495-1525:
- 11:00:06.459Z: an assistant API error rate_limit, "You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 4:50pm (Asia/Jerusalem)".
- 11:00:06.462Z: system informational "Usage limit reached · continuing automatically at 4:50pm · esc to cancel". This is Claude Code's own auto-continue wait.
- 11:00:06.466Z: "moe-account-switch: its classic.StopFailure hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it." The skip is the same as in 05e1f916.
- 11:00:16.545Z: queue-operation enqueue "/exit", then dequeue at 11:00:16.553. So 05e1f916's turn.complete checkHardLimit fallback fired, and leave() ran $.command.run({command:'exit'}) EXIT_DELAY_MS later.
- The session did NOT end. A background-task notification queued at 11:10:00 stayed pending.
- At 12:23:31Z the /exit finally shows as executed, with "<local-command-stdout>(no content)". The process kept running, the queued notification started a new turn, and that turn hit rate_limit again.
- At 14:51:06Z: "Usage limit reset · Continuing automatically" and "Your claude.ai usage limit has reset. Continue the task you were working on…". The seat resumed on the SAME account, about 3h50m after the limit.
- The wrapper never relaunched it on the next account, which was available all along. VSC-17 sat unplanned the whole time, and with it the VS Code epic's integration row VSC-18.

**Likely cause.** The engine documents $.command.run as "queued and run once the session is idle" and "Rejects … past a Stop or a host's limit" (scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/.claude-plugin/types/claude-code/index.d.ts, around line 3180). Claude Code's limit auto-continue wait keeps the session from going idle, so the mod's /exit (register.ts exit() at line 130, scheduled from leave() at line 143) waits behind it. When it finally runs, it does not end the session. The same auto-continue is what the 10-24 incident in 05e1f916 "sat idle until".

**Scope.** This affects every interactive seat (architect and governor TUIs) whose leased account hits a hard limit mid-turn. Headless seats are unaffected, because their wrapper detects the failed run. Today it cost about 3h50m on one seat. It is the second observed occurrence of this class: 10-24 2h41m, and 11-02.

**Suggested direction (the architect decides; confirm the engine behaviour with the plugin-authoring skill first):**
- (a) In the mod: on a hard limit, get the session idle before /exit. Cancel the auto-continue wait, the "esc to cancel" path, if the engine exposes it (turn.abort, a prompt or session op). Or end the session by a route that does not queue behind it.
- (b) Make the auto-continue impossible for leased interactive seats: a Claude Code setting the wrapper passes via --settings. That is the wrapper lane (moe-agent.sh/ps1 twins), so prefer (a) if it works.
- (c) As a backstop, the wrapper's heartbeat sidecar or account sampler could notice its leased account at 100% while the interactive CLI still runs, and end the CLI so the loop relaunches on the next account. That is also the wrapper lane.

**Evidence to keep:** the transcript lines above, and the acct-2 usage sample /mnt/c/Users/Yaron/.moe/claude-usage/acct-2.json (refusedUntil 14:50Z).
definitionOfDone: A leased interactive seat whose main turn ends at a hard usage limit while Claude Code shows its limit auto-continue wait ends its session, so the wrapper loop relaunches it on the next account. Proven by a test that models the auto-continue state (or the engine's equivalent) and fails on HEAD.

The existing paths keep working: the StopFailure path, 05e1f916's turn.complete fallback, accountSwitch, END_SESSION and idle. No exit is scheduled for a subagent turn, a session without MOE_WORKER_ID/MOE_ACCOUNT_ID, or a turn with every window below 100%.

Fresh `claude plugin test scripts/mods/moe-account-switch` passes, and its output is supplied to complete_task. If the fix touches scripts/moe-agent.sh or .ps1, both twins change together and parity-check.sh passes.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement the fix in hooks/register.ts. Keep the file loadable at every save: live architect and governor TUIs load this folder from the checkout through CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS.

Verified root cause (claude 2.1.316 binary; acct-2 transcript 401f548a):
- The mod's /exit DID run at 11:00:16: enqueue, then dequeue 8 ms later.
- claude's /exit command renders 'Background work is running' instead of shutting down whenever a background shell, subagent, workflow, monitor, MCP task or session cron is running (a worktree session gets its own dialog). Its choices are Exit and stop tasks / Move to background and exit / Stay, and it has no timeout. The architect's run_in_background CI Bash (bf1lp10b7) was running at the time.
- Its '(no content)' row was written at 12:23:31, when the dialog was dismissed.
- `session.exiting` latched for the whole session. After the 14:51 resume, the stale 11:00 pending refused claim_next_task while leave() returned silently.
- The auto-continue wait itself does not block /exit: transcript 494b2898 shows 'Claude Code exited during the wait'.

Changes:
1. export const FORCE_EXIT_DELAY_MS = 60_000.
2. Track a running main turn: main turn.start sets it, main turn.complete clears it.
3. `exiting` means 'an exit attempt is in flight'. Every attempt that ends without ending the session clears it, so the next main turn.complete (aborted or not) starts a new attempt (leave()'s toast, /exit after EXIT_DELAY_MS) while `pending` holds.
4. exit() first names this CLI.
   - Windows (session cwd matches /^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|\\\\)/): the PowerShell argv below.
   - Otherwise: $.process.run(['sh','-c','echo "$PPID"'], {timeoutMs: 5_000}). The child's parent is this CLI, because $.process.run spawns argv directly; a probe mod on 11-02 printed the claude PID. Accept only a safe integer > 1, giving ['sh','-c','kill -TERM "$1"','sh', String(pid)].
   Then arm the fallback with $.clock.after(FORCE_EXIT_DELAY_MS, ...), then await $.command.run({command:'exit'}).
   - A rejection ends the attempt with the manual toast, as today, and no termination. claude refuses or holds a plugin's input after a person's Stop (Esc).
   - A resolution does NOT cancel the fallback. A person's Stay, or a background-kind session that only detaches, must not park the seat.
5. When the fallback fires:
   - if the attempt is already over, do nothing;
   - if a main turn is running, re-arm FORCE_EXIT_DELAY_MS;
   - otherwise run $.process.run(argv, {timeoutMs: 30_000}).
   Exit code 0 means delivered: SIGTERM runs claude's own shutdown, which stops the session's background tasks and exits 143. No argv, a non-zero exit or a rejection shows the ending's manual toast and ends the attempt. If the CLI still runs FORCE_EXIT_DELAY_MS after a delivered termination, end the attempt the same way.
6. Windows argv: ['powershell.exe','-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-Command', SCRIPT].
   Copy SCRIPT exactly. It is 676 chars with no double quotes, because Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops them under -Command (task-76d4500a). It was live-tested on PS 5.1.26100 from WSL: it stopped its parent stand-in and that parent's background ping, and nothing else.
$all = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process); $self = $all | Where-Object { $_.ProcessId -eq $PID }; $cli = $all | Where-Object { $_.ProcessId -eq $self.ParentProcessId -and $_.CreationDate -le $self.CreationDate }; if ($null -eq $cli) { exit 3 }; $doomed = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList; function Add-Tree($p) { foreach ($c in $all) { if ($c.ParentProcessId -eq $p.ProcessId -and $c.ProcessId -ne $PID -and $c.Name -ne 'conhost.exe' -and $c.CreationDate -ge $p.CreationDate) { Add-Tree $c; [void]$doomed.Add($c.ProcessId) } } }; Add-Tree $cli; foreach ($id in $doomed) { Stop-Process -Id $id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Stop-Process -Id $cli.ProcessId -Force

Error handling: every new $ call (session.cwd, process.run, clock.after, command.run, ui.toast) stays inside try/catch and fails open to the ending's existing manual toast. No hook or timer may throw.
Rewrite the module's top comment for the new end route, and add a short why-comment at each non-obvious line: the dialog, PPID = this CLI, SIGTERM and exit 143, the quote-free script.
Run the suite. All tests from step 1 must pass, along with the 53 existing ones.
implementationPlan.note:
I rewrote hooks/register.ts in a single Write, so the live TUIs never loaded a half-edited module.

New pieces:
- `export const FORCE_EXIT_DELAY_MS = 60_000`.
- `Session` has `running` (set by main turn.start, cleared by main turn.complete before any awaited call) and `attempt?: Attempt`, which replaces the `exiting` latch.
- `Attempt` holds `{ending, argv?, timer?: Timer, delivered}`.

How an attempt runs:
- `leave()` creates the attempt, toasts and arms the 10 s exit. Its toast and timer are now in a try; a throw clears the attempt so the next turn retries.
- `exit()` names the CLI first (`nameCli`), arms the fallback before /exit, then awaits /exit. A rejection calls `giveUp`, which shows the manual toast. A resolution keeps the fallback armed.
- `force()` (the fallback):
  - does nothing once its attempt is over;
  - gives up if a termination was already delivered;
  - re-arms while a main turn is running;
  - gives up if there is no argv;
  - otherwise runs process.run(argv, 30 s). After the await it re-checks that the attempt is still current. A non-zero exit gives up. Exit 0 marks the attempt delivered and arms the post-kill check.
- `giveUp()` is idempotent per attempt: it clears the attempt, toasts MANUAL[ending] (the same three texts as before) and cancels the timer.

Naming the CLI:
- On Windows (`/^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|\\\\)/` matches the session cwd) it uses the powershell.exe argv with STOP_CLI_PS. That script is byte-identical to the plan: a node comparison against the plan text found 676 chars, no double quote and no backslash.
- Otherwise it runs `sh -c 'echo "$PPID"'` with a 5 s timeout and accepts only exit 0 with stdout matching /^\d+$/, a safe integer > 1. The argv uses String(Number(pid)).

Every new `$` call is inside a try, and nothing can throw out of a hook or timer. The top comment and the why-comments are updated.

I also tightened the step-1 (f) tests. At the exact fallback time they now assert that a failed termination toasts at once, while a delivered one waits a full delay. Before this, the 'kill exit code ignored' mutant was caught by only 1 test; now 4 catch it.

Evidence:
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) claude plugin test scripts/mods/moe-account-switch`: 92 pass, 0 fail.
- Mutant sweep in scratch /tmp/tmp.43mI3PwKzJ (fail counts): no running check 1; never clearing the attempt 2; pid 1 accepted 3; cancel on /exit resolve 5; no delivered check 4; kill exit ignored 4 after tightening; no Windows branch 2.
- tsc: moe-vscode's TS 6.0.2 reports only baseline TS5097/TS2769, both in the test file. register.ts is clean.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's diff (load adversarial-self-review). Read it as an attacker:
- Could the mod signal anything but its own CLI? Check: the PID is captured just before /exit from a $.process.run child while the CLI is alive; it is a safe integer > 1; $PPID is never read at kill time; there is no name or pattern match. On Windows: a creation-time-checked parent and its descendants only, with the helper and conhost.exe skipped.
- Can it terminate without a decided ending? Check: a subagent turn, a -p run, a below-100% window, a missing seat id. Only exit() may arm the fallback, and exit() only follows leave() with pending set.
- Concurrency. Check: two endings; repeated turn.complete or StopFailure; a turn starting inside the 10 s or 60 s windows; the fallback racing a late /exit or a person answering the dialog. At most one attempt is in flight, each attempt terminates at most once, and no timer is left armed after an attempt ends.
- A hot reload drops state and timers. It must fail safe: no termination.
- A failing cwd read, capture or process.run ends the attempt with the manual toast. Nothing throws, and there are no unhandled rejections.
- The Windows script must be byte-identical to the plan. If you changed it, re-run a probe in a scratch dir outside the checkout: a stand-in parent powershell starts a background ping and runs the script as its own child, and both must be gone afterwards. Kill only PIDs your probe started.
- Note the accepted edge: a seat terminated less than 120 s after its launch is classed as a wrapper launch failure (MOE_LAUNCH_FAIL_SEC).

If anything changes, re-run step 4's exact command and submit that fresh output.
implementationPlan.note:
I reviewed this task's own diff as an attacker (git diff on the 4 paths only). Nothing changed, so step 4's fresh run stands: 92 pass, 0 fail.

Signals only its own CLI:
- The PID is read from a $.process.run child's $PPID inside exit(), just before /exit. It must be exit 0, /^\d+$/, a safe integer and > 1. Nothing reads $PPID at kill time, and nothing matches by name or pattern.
- The mod runs inside the CLI, so if the fallback timer fires at all, the CLI is still alive and the captured PID is still its own; it cannot have been reused.
- If $.process.run ever went through a helper process, $PPID would name that helper, which is a child of the CLI. The kill would then leave the CLI up, and the post-kill check would show the manual toast. That fails safe.
- Windows: STOP_CLI_PS is byte-identical to the plan (676 chars, no `"`), so no new probe was needed. It only targets its parent, checked by creation time, and that parent's later-created descendants, skipping its own $PID and conhost.exe.

No termination without a decided ending:
- force() is armed only in exit(). exit() runs only from leave()'s timer, and leave() requires `pending`.
- The (i) tests cover a subagent turn, a missing MOE_WORKER_ID or MOE_ACCOUNT_ID, and every window below 100%. A -p run cannot set the END_SESSION pending (surfaces check, unchanged).

Concurrency:
- At most one attempt runs, because leave() returns while `session.attempt` is set. The first signal still wins (`??=`).
- Each attempt terminates at most once. There is a single kill site, and after it either `delivered` is set (the next check gives up rather than re-kill) or giveUp runs.
- One timer per attempt: re-arming happens only inside the firing force(), and no timer is armed while the kill is awaited.
- giveUp cancels the attempt's timer. A late /exit rejection racing an in-flight kill clears the attempt. force() re-checks `session.attempt` after its await and returns.
- An older attempt's /exit settling late is a no-op, because giveUp is guarded by attempt identity.
- A turn that starts inside the 10 s or 60 s window: command.run queues until idle, and force() re-arms every 60 s while a main turn runs.

Hot reload: the engine documents that a hot reload cancels the plugin's pending waits (index.d.ts, the `clock` doc). The new module starts with no pending and no attempt, so there is no termination.

Failure paths: nameCli, giveUp, force and exit catch every `$` call, and leave() wraps its toast and timer and clears the attempt on a throw. `void exit/force` cannot reject, so there are no unhandled rejections.

Theoretical, noted but not fixed:
- If another plugin swallowed main turn.complete, or denied turn.start, `running` could stick true. The fallback would then re-arm forever, which is the same as HEAD's behaviour, no worse.
- A person who deliberately chose Stay is still ended 60 s after /exit, by plan design.
- Accepted edge: a seat terminated less than 120 s after launch is classed as a launch failure (MOE_LAUNCH_FAIL_SEC).

comments.author: architect-93e0e956
comments.content:
Planner, 15:5xZ, re @governor-e6b40560's 15:36Z note. Both data points are covered by the plan (rev 1, 5 steps).

1. The 11:00 stall was not the auto-continue. The mod's /exit ran at 11:00:16 (enqueued, then dequeued 8 ms later). claude 2.1.316's /exit opens a "Background work is running" dialog (Exit and stop tasks / Move to background and exit / Stay; no timeout) whenever background work is running: a shell, subagent, monitor, MCP task or session cron. The seat's run_in_background CI Bash (bf1lp10b7) was running. The '(no content)' row at 12:23:31 is that dialog being dismissed. 494b2898 shows /exit can end a session during the limit wait ("exited during the wait").

2. The 14:57 stall: the submit_plan reply at 14:56:45 carried no accountSwitch. claim_next_task was refused by the stale 11:00 hard-limit `pending`, and `session.exiting` had latched at 11:00:06. So leave() returned before scheduling or toasting anything. There was no toast; the human found the seat on their own.

Fix, mod-only (no wrapper twins):
- The mod records its own CLI PID just before /exit, using a $.process.run child's $PPID; a probe on 11-02 matched the claude PID. If the CLI still runs 60 s later with no main turn running, the mod sends it SIGTERM: claude's own shutdown, exit 143, and the wrapper relaunches the seat on the next account. On Windows a quote-free PowerShell 5.1 script does the same; I tested it live from WSL.
- The exiting latch is now per attempt. A refused /exit, or a termination that fails, ends that attempt with the 'Type /exit' toast, and the next main turn.complete (aborted or not) starts a new attempt.
- The tests include your path: an aborted turn, then turn.complete, then a second /exit. That test fails on HEAD.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When the moe-account-switch mod has decided to end an interactive seat's session (account switch or hard usage limit, END_SESSION, idle), the session ends even when claude's /exit does not end it. claude's /exit opens 'Background work is running' over running background work; it has no timeout and waits for a person. On 11-02 a seat sat behind it, in the usage-limit auto-continue wait, for 3h50m. The mod names its own CLI before /exit. 60 s after /exit, once no main turn is running, it terminates that CLI: POSIX SIGTERM runs claude's shutdown and exits 143; on Windows a quote-free PowerShell script stops the CLI's descendants, then the CLI. The wrapper loop then relaunches the seat, on the next account in the account case. A refused /exit (claude holds a plugin's input after a person's Stop) or a failed termination ends that attempt with today's 'Type /exit' toast. The next main turn that completes starts a new attempt, so a pending ending never sits silent. That covers task comment 15:36Z: after the 14:51 resume the stale 11:00 pending refused claim_next_task while leave() returned without scheduling anything.
acceptanceCriteria: A leased seat whose main turn ends at a hard limit, with StopFailure skipped and its /exit never returning (the auto-continue wait plus the background-work exit dialog), has its own CLI terminated exactly once, 60 s after /exit. The test for this fails on HEAD.
After an attempt that did not end the session (refused /exit, failed termination), the next main turn.complete, aborted or not, schedules a new toast and /exit. The test for this fails on HEAD.

The StopFailure path, the turn.complete fallback, accountSwitch, END_SESSION and idle keep their toasts, refusals and 10 s /exit. A subagent turn, a session without MOE_WORKER_ID/MOE_ACCOUNT_ID, or every window below 100% gets no exit, PID capture or termination.
Fresh `claude plugin test scripts/mods/moe-account-switch` passes, and its output is the complete_task evidence. No wrapper twin changes.
invariants: Only a session whose ending the mod already decided (session.pending set and leave() ran) is ever terminated. At most one attempt is in flight, and each attempt terminates at most once.

Only this CLI is signalled: the PID that its own $.process.run child reported as its parent, captured just before /exit while the CLI is alive (a safe integer > 1). Never by name or pattern. On Windows, only this CLI and its own descendants (ParentProcessId with creation-time ordering; the helper and conhost.exe skipped).
No termination while a main turn is running; the fallback waits for the turn to end.
Every engine call on the new path fails open, to the ending's manual /exit toast. No exception escapes a hook or timer.
compatibility: No MCP tool, daemon or wrapper change. scripts/moe-agent.sh and .ps1 are untouched, so parity-check.sh is not owed.
Existing toasts, HELD refusals, the 10 s /exit timing, first-signal-wins and the END_SESSION/idle gates are unchanged. FORCE_EXIT_DELAY_MS is a new export.

A terminated POSIX seat exits 143. The wrapper's account_after_exit and the next lease treat that like any exit, and the lease skips the spent account. Only a run shorter than MOE_LAUNCH_FAIL_SEC (120 s) would be classed as a launch failure.

Only with none does it call the shutdown. Seen in transcript 401f548a: background Bash bf1lp10b7 running at 11:00:16, and /exit's '(no content)' row written at 12:23:31.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- (a) As filed, cancel the limit auto-continue: rejected. The engine has no op for it, and it is not what blocks /exit: transcript 494b2898 (11:49Z) shows 'Automatic continue cancelled · Claude Code exited during the wait'. The blocker is claude's background-work exit dialog.
- (b) A --settings opt-out: rejected. It is wrapper lane and does not touch the dialog.
- (c) A wrapper backstop kill: robust, but wrapper lane (sh+ps1, parity, postflight), serialized behind open WT/CQ rows. The mod can do the same from inside, with a PID it is sure of.
- Stop background tasks before /exit via TaskStop/CronDelete: rejected. There is no task-registry op, and each new item kind would silently re-break it.
- Answer the dialog: there is no engine op for that.
- SIGINT (exit 0): rejected in favour of SIGTERM, the stable terminate contract (claude's handler is shutdown(143)).
- Cancel the fallback when /exit resolves, to respect Stay: rejected. Whether a dialog command's $.command.run resolves at completion or at dispatch cannot be observed, and a dispatch-time resolution would silently disable the fix. Only a refused /exit (the engine's own hold after a person's Stop) cancels it.
- Kill $PPID at kill time: rejected for a capture just before /exit. Reparenting to a subreaper (WSL init, systemd --user) during a concurrent exit could otherwise hit the wrong process.
